description: Point the tenant's Twilio WhatsApp sender at CallPilotAI's inbound webhook, so customer replies land in the lead timeline. Without it the inbound endpoint exists but stays silent — Twilio does not know where to send. Finds the sender whose number EXACTLY matches the stored WhatsApp sender (never 'the first one'), reads its current webhook, sets it and reads back what Twilio reports. dry_run: true only reads. Needs the Twilio connection with Auth Token and a stored sender (set_whatsapp_provider sender=…). Webhook addresses are returned masked (query values and credentials as ***); the previous one is kept in the vault, so zuruecksetzen: true restores it (with dry_run: true only shows what would be set).

dry_run.description: Only read the current webhook (or what a restore would set), change nothing.

restore_url.description: Way back with an explicit https address instead of the stored one. Prefer zuruecksetzen: true - a webhook URL often carries another system's key.

zuruecksetzen.description: Way back: set the sender's webhook back to the address it had before connect_whatsapp_inbound changed it. That address was stored in the vault at connect time and is never shown (only masked).

name: connect_whatsapp_inbound
